CurrentUserResponse.description: What we tell the frontend about the currently logged-in user.
CurrentUserResponse.title: CurrentUserResponse

InterventionRequestCreateRequest.description:
What's sent to create a brand-new intervention request.

request_number and submitted_at are never accepted here — both are
computed by the endpoint itself (see create_intervention_request).
InterventionRequestCreateRequest.title: InterventionRequestCreateRequest

InterventionRequestResponse.description: One intervention request, as shown on the Intervention Requests screen.
InterventionRequestResponse.title: InterventionRequestResponse

InterventionRequestUpdateRequest.description:
What's sent to update an existing intervention request — same shape
as creating one (request_number/submitted_at stay fixed once set).
InterventionRequestUpdateRequest.title: InterventionRequestUpdateRequest

InterventionRequestsDashboardResponse.description:
Aggregate KPI stats for Intervention Requests' landing dashboard
("KPI overview").
InterventionRequestsDashboardResponse.title: InterventionRequestsDashboardResponse

InterventionRequestsStatusBreakdownItem.description:
One status, with how many intervention requests currently carry it —
one bar of the KPI dashboard's status breakdown chart.
InterventionRequestsStatusBreakdownItem.title: InterventionRequestsStatusBreakdownItem

InterventionRequestsTeamBreakdownItem.description:
One team/association name, with how many intervention requests were
logged for it — one bar of the KPI dashboard's team breakdown chart.
InterventionRequestsTeamBreakdownItem.title: InterventionRequestsTeamBreakdownItem

InterventionRequestsTeamResponse.description:
One MasterData team, as shown in the Intervention Requests screen's
"Ploeg" dropdown — just enough to populate it (id + name), read
directly from MasterData_team (see app/db/models/team.py) rather than
MasterData's own TeamResponse, so Intervention Requests users can
always pick a team regardless of whether they also have a MasterData
role (see the "teams" endpoint in module_3/router.py).
InterventionRequestsTeamResponse.title: InterventionRequestsTeamResponse

InterventionStatusResponse.description: One status, as shown on the Intervention Statuses screen.
InterventionStatusResponse.title: InterventionStatusResponse

KarActionCreateRequest.description:
What's sent to log one kar movement. The team and timestamp are filled
in by the server, never by the client.
KarActionCreateRequest.title: KarActionCreateRequest

KarActionKarOption.description:
One entry of the "Manuele kar beweging" kar dropdown: the kar plus its
current team (shown read-only, logged as snapshot) and current status
(used to pre-select the status dropdown).
KarActionKarOption.title: KarActionKarOption

KarActionResponse.description: One logged kar movement, with the names needed for the history table.
KarActionResponse.title: KarActionResponse

KarMapAfleverlocatieRow.description:
One delivery location's pin/list entry on the Kar Map screen,
joined with its zone and distribution point names.
KarMapAfleverlocatieRow.title: KarMapAfleverlocatieRow

KarMapDistributiepuntRow.description: One distribution point's pin/list entry on the Kar Map screen.
KarMapDistributiepuntRow.title: KarMapDistributiepuntRow

KarMapKarRow.description:
One kar's pin/list entry on the Kar Map screen — KarManagement
joined with its status/team lookups for the popup's "resume" content.
KarMapKarRow.title: KarMapKarRow

KarMapResponse.description:
The full Kar Map payload: one array per layer. Rows with no
latitude/longitude are included too — the frontend excludes them from
the map itself but still lists them in the side panel.
KarMapResponse.title: KarMapResponse

KarPlanningFestivalResponse.description: One festival column of the Kar Planning report.
KarPlanningFestivalResponse.title: KarPlanningFestivalResponse

KarPlanningReportResponse.description:
The whole Kar Planning report: the active festivals of the requested
season (one extra table column each, in start-date order) plus one row
per kar. `festivals` is empty when no season was requested.
KarPlanningReportResponse.title: KarPlanningReportResponse

KarPlanningResponse.description:
One kar, denormalized by joining KarManagement with its status/team/
transport-type lookups — the first query in what will grow into a
wider, multi-table Kar Planning report as more tables are added.
KarPlanningResponse.title: KarPlanningResponse

KarTrackerGroundplanResponse.description:
One ground-plan overlay: its name and south-west/north-east corner
coordinates. The image itself is served separately by
GET /groundplans/{id}/image; updated_at lets the frontend cache-bust
that URL after the image is replaced.
KarTrackerGroundplanResponse.title: KarTrackerGroundplanResponse

LoginRequest.description: What the frontend must send us to log a user in.
LoginRequest.title: LoginRequest

MobileKarScanResponse.description: The kar found for a scanned QR code, with its latest movements.
MobileKarScanResponse.title: MobileKarScanResponse

MobileModule2PermissionsResponse.description:
What the calling user may do in the phone's KarTracker: KarScan (the
web's "Manuele kar beweging"), Kar Planning and Kar Map. There is no
delete flag: deleting a movement is web-only.
MobileModule2PermissionsResponse.title: MobileModule2PermissionsResponse

MobileModule3LookupsResponse.description: Every dropdown list the request form needs, in one round trip.
MobileModule3LookupsResponse.title: MobileModule3LookupsResponse

MobileModule3PermissionsResponse.description:
What the calling user may do on the phone's Intervention Requests
"Akties" screen, so the app only shows buttons the web roles allow.
(There is no delete flag: deleting is web-only.)
MobileModule3PermissionsResponse.title: MobileModule3PermissionsResponse

MobileRefreshRequest.description:
What the phone sends to swap its refresh token for a fresh pair.

The web app keeps this token in a cookie; the phone has no cookie jar,
so it stores the token in the device's secure storage and sends it here.
MobileRefreshRequest.title: MobileRefreshRequest

MobileSeasonResponse.description: One open season, for the phone's Kar Planning season dropdown.
MobileSeasonResponse.title: MobileSeasonResponse

MobileTokenResponse.description: The tokens (plus who the user is) handed back after login/refresh.
MobileTokenResponse.title: MobileTokenResponse

ModuleResponse.description: One module/tile, as shown on the landing page.
ModuleResponse.title: ModuleResponse

PlanKarOption.description: One entry of a "Plan a kar" dropdown (a team or a delivery location).
PlanKarOption.title: PlanKarOption

TeamKarMemberOptionResponse.description:
One current TeamKar member, as shown in the Intervention Requests
screen's "Team Kar" dropdown — just enough to populate it (id + name).
Gated by Intervention Requests' own "requests" screen permission, not
TeamKar's own, the same reasoning as the "teams" endpoint below: a user
can always pick a Team Kar member here regardless of whether they also
have the TeamKar screen's permission.
TeamKarMemberOptionResponse.title: TeamKarMemberOptionResponse

post.description: Check an email/password combination and hand back tokens in the body.
Revoke the phone's refresh token so it can never be used again.

get.description: Who is logged in, and which modules can they open (Bearer token required).

get.description: The ground plans overlaid on the Kar Map: name and corner coordinates.

get.description: One ground plan's image bytes (PNG or JPEG).

post.description:
Log one kar movement, exactly like the web's Save button: the team and
timestamp are set here, and the kar's latest status/location follow.

get.description:
Every kar, afleverlocatie and distributiepunt for the map, identical
to the web's Kar Map data (rows without coordinates included).

The Kar Planning report, identical to the web's; with a season, one
planned afleverlocatie per active festival of it.

The status dropdown, gated by the movement screen itself (like the
web's /kar-actions/lookups) so no KarStatussen rights are needed.

get.description:
The kar whose QR code was scanned, plus its last few movements.

The scanned text is trimmed and matched case-insensitively, so a QR code
printed as "b001 " still finds kar "B001".

What this user may do in the phone's KarTracker, so the app only
shows the menu items and buttons the web roles allow.

The open seasons (the same ones the web header's season selector
offers), newest first, for the Kar Planning season dropdown.

schema.title: Response List Open Seasons Api Mobile V1 Module 2 Seasons Get

get.description: The KPI overview numbers, gated only by module access like on the web.

Every request, newest first; open_only=true keeps only requests
whose status is an "open" one (the web screen's default filter).

schema.title: Response List Intervention Requests Api Mobile V1 Module 3 Intervention Requests Get

post.description: Create a request. Its number and timestamp are set here, never by the app.

get.description: One request, for the phone's detail/edit screen.

put.description: Update every editable field (number and timestamp stay fixed).

get.description:
The statuses, teams and TeamKar members for the request form.

Gated by the requests screen's own permission (not the MasterData
"statuses" screen), so anyone who can see requests can always name and
pick a status, exactly like the web's teams/TeamKar dropdown endpoints.
What this user may do on the requests screen (view / create / edit).

The landing-page tiles for this user, in tile order.

A module appears only if (1) the phone supports it, (2) it is switched
on site-wide, and (3) the super admin granted this user access to it.
Being super admin does not grant access by itself, exactly like the web.
